paper_title: DTaPO: Dynamic Thermal-Aware Performance Optimization for Dark Silicon Many-Core Systems

scenario.figure_or_table: Section 4.1 experimental setup, Figure 4, Tables 2-4 and Figure 10 (64-core DTaPO evaluation with radix, ocean, blackscholes, bodytrack)
scenario.description: DTaPO dynamic thermal management (task migration plus DVFS) evaluated on a 64-core NoC many-core system with 32 active and 32 dark cores in a chessboard pattern. Each core tile is 2.95 mm x 2.95 mm. Power is computed per core with McPAT (22 nm) and passed to HotSpot (L3 power excluded). Temperature thresholds range from 60 to 85 C. The paper gives no per-block coordinates and no per-core power values in watts, so no complete floorplan-and-power experiment can be extracted. No code, data or repository links were found in the paper.
scenario.architecture: 64-core homogeneous 22 nm many-core, 8x8 mesh NoC, 4 GHz max frequency, 32 KB L1-I, 32 KB L1-D, 512 KB private L2 per core, 8 MB L3 shared per 8-core cluster, 50% of cores active in chessboard pattern, HotSpot CBGA-style stacked package (silicon 0.15 mm, TIM 20 um at 4 W/mK, spreader, heat sink, ambient 318.15 K)
scenario.workload: Mix of four 8-thread applications: radix and ocean (SPLASH-2), blackscholes and bodytrack (PARSEC); 32 active cores, 32 dark cores
scenario.operating_point: Threshold temperatures Tthr 60-85 C, safe margin epsilon 5 C, frequency step 200 MHz, Fthr 3.6 GHz, max 4 GHz; results averaged over ten runs; transient temperature reported as max/avg/min (90th/10th percentile) per Figure 10

original_setup.solver: LifeSim toolchain (Sniper performance traces, McPAT 22 nm power, HotSpot 6.0 transient compact thermal model). HotSpot uses a stacked CBGA-style package: 0.15 mm silicon, 20 um TIM at 4 W/mK, heat spreader, heat sink, ambient 318.15 K. Evaluated on a 64-core, 8x8 mesh NoC system with 32 active and 32 dark cores in a chessboard pattern, with 2.95 mm x 2.95 mm cores.
original_setup.optimizer: DTaPO threshold-based heuristic (Algorithm 1, Eq. 3) that minimizes makespan subject to Ti < Tthr for all cores. It is not a mathematical optimizer.
original_setup.controller: Periodic run-time DTM combining one-way cluster-based task migration from hot active cores to dark cores in the same L3 cluster with stepwise DVFS. Parameters: safe margin epsilon 5 C, frequency step 200 MHz, Fthr 3.6 GHz, max 4 GHz, Tthr 60-85 C, 100 us wake-up latency, 1000-cycle migration penalty.
original_setup.benchmark: Four 8-thread applications on 64 cores: radix and ocean (SPLASH-2), blackscholes and bodytrack (PARSEC). Compared against no DTM, DVFS-only and a re-implemented OSP (TDP 42 W). Results are averaged over ten runs.

thermal_observable.location: Per-core transient temperature across the 64-core chip. Peak, average and minimum/maximum core temperatures are reported in Figure 10 and as peak chip temperature in Figures 9 and 12. The text states an average peak temperature reduction of up to 10.8 C versus DVFS-only. No absolute value is stated in the text.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum (90th percentile), average and minimum (10th percentile) of transient core temperatures over the run, averaged over ten runs and four applications. Per-threshold absolute values appear only in the Figure 10 chart and are not digitized here.

physical_mismatches.reason: The paper gives no per-block x/y coordinates and no per-core power in watts for any scenario. Only the core tile size (2.95 mm) and the 64-core, 8x8 layout are stated, so a complete floorplan-and-power experiment cannot be built.

The scenario is dynamic and closed-loop. Power changes over time with task migration, DVFS and core wake-up, and the observable is a transient temperature trace. A steady-state, single-power-map thermal model cannot reproduce the controller behavior or the transient percentile statistics.

The workload-driven power traces come from Sniper and McPAT. L3 cache power is excluded from the HotSpot input, and the dark cores are modeled with static power only. Any static power map would not match this time-varying, workload-dependent power.
The detailed HotSpot package (CBGA-style stack, heat sink convection R and C, ambient 318.15 K) may differ from a bundled Studio package, so absolute temperatures are not directly comparable.

The setup is a 2D single-die system. No 3D stacking, interposer, liquid cooling or reliability model is used in the evaluation (LifeSim is a lifetime-reliability tool, but no reliability result is reported).
